reasons: Claimed status is compliant and consistent with the artifacts: no redline and no counterparty comment were produced, so nothing is being raised as a negotiation issue.

The cited paragraphs support the rationale — §6 (documentation on request) and §3(e) (real-time usage statistics/log access) run in Customer's favour, and §8(f) is a narrow anti-spamming technical-measures right, not a usage audit with frequency, notice, cost-allocation or system-access exposure.

AUDIT is a protective cap on Vendor audit rights; silence is at least as favourable as the preferred position, so inserting audit parameters would gratuitously create a right TrueLink does not have. Treating this as compliant rather than 'missing' is correct under the instruction not to flag terms benefiting our party.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' regex is explained as a heuristic artefact of there being no audit clause to carry a frequency limit; no unaddressed risk is left open, and the rationale records the preferred/fallback parameters to demand if TrueLink later seeks an audit right.
